title: Bijectivity of the extended representing counit
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of positive prime characteristic different from $\ell$, separated finite-type $k$-schemes $X,Y$, a $k$-morphism $f:X\to Y$, and a compactification $c$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Write $\mathcal C_H(T)$ and $\mathcal C_\Omega(T)$ for the bounded constructible condensed module-object categories and scalar functors $T^T_{H,H'}$, $T^T_{H,\Omega}$ of [prop-weil-pbc-qbar-condensed-two-colimit], with $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ carrying the finite-subextension-valued condensed coefficient ring. Write $P_H$ and $P_\Omega$ for the fixed compact-support composites [lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization]. The data structures and displayed equations are [def-pur-filtered-condensed-representing-pair-data]. Suppose $s$ is a canonical scalar comparison family and $d=(M,L,t,\beta)$ is a supplied compatible representing pair at a finite coefficient field $E$: $t:P_E M\to L$ and finite-overfield Hom equivalences $\beta$ determined by its scalar extensions as in Pair.IsCompatible. Put $M_\Omega=T^X_{E,\Omega}M$, $L_\Omega=T^Y_{E,\Omega}L$ and $t_\Omega=T^Y_{E,\Omega}(t)\circ s_{E,\Omega,M}^{-1}$. For every $C\in\mathcal C_\Omega(X)$ the explicitly defined map $\operatorname{Hom}(C,M_\Omega)\to\operatorname{Hom}(P_\Omega C,L_\Omega)$, $u\mapsto t_\Omega\circ P_\Omega(u)$, is bijective. This asserts only bijectivity of that map, not any adjunction or transpose conclusion.

proof.text:
finite type over a field makes X and Y Noetherian. Apply the recorded
constructible two-colimit on each scheme. Fields containing E are cofinal, since
a compositum with E is again finite. Model C at one such field H. For a morphism
from P(C) to the extended L, the projection comparison identifies its source with
the extension of P_H(C_H). Morphism descent on Y gives a representative at a
larger common field. Its inverse under the supplied finite beta extends to a
preimage by counit_finite_formula, proving surjectivity. For injectivity, descend
two maps on X simultaneously. Equality of their counit images descends on Y after
a further enlargement. The finite formula and finite beta injectivity give equality
of their representatives there and hence equality over the closure. Transport both
arguments along the model isomorphism and its support image. The same argument
covers zero objects and the empty scheme; no arbitrary model enters the map itself.
